title: Ephemeral Guardian Access Protocols and Post-Incident Audit Playbook
creator: Ari Sharma
description:
Proposal for a formalized, least-privilege emergency access flow ("Guardian Access") tied into RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML, plus mandatory post-incident auditing. 

Problem: Current emergency elevation mechanisms are ad-hoc, long-lived, and lack consistent audit signals.

Goal: Ship an ephemeral, auditable break-glass channel that: (1) grants time-limited elevated roles via RBAC v2, (2) requires dual approval or an automated escalation policy, (3) integrates with SSO/SAML for identity provenance, (4) emits structured audit events to the central logging pipeline, and (5) triggers an automatic post-incident review checklist and rotation actions.

Scope: Server-side procedures, console controls, short-lived guardian tokens, admin session recording metadata, automated rotation hooks, and the post-incident audit playbook. Out of scope: long-term policy changes to product RBAC mappings (will be tracked separately).
acceptance_criteria: Guardian access can be requested from Console and CLI and requires one of: two human approvals (on-call + security) or an automated guardrail condition (incident severity >= P0)
Issued guardian sessions are time-limited (default 15 minutes) and support renewal only with fresh approval; all renewals are logged
All guardian issuance and session events are emitted as structured JSON to the audit-log stream with enforced schema (actor, reason, approvers, TTL, scopes, request_id)
SSO/SAML assertion is validated and recorded; fallback OOB verification exists for off-network emergency requests
Playbook automation creates a post-incident review ticket with links to session logs, diff of role bindings, and any objects modified during the elevated session
KMS-backed signing for temporary tokens is implemented and keys are rotated per rotation policy triggered after any guardian use
E2E tests covering request -> approval -> session -> audit emission -> post-incident ticket creation are added to the CI pipeline
implementation_steps: Design: finalize approval model (two-person vs automated policy) and the guardian scope model within RBAC v2 (scoped role templates)
Backend: implement guardian issue API with TTL, approver workflow, and KMS-signed ephemeral credentials
SSO: extend SAML assertion handler to attach assertion metadata to guardian sessions and reject unsigned assertions
Audit: add structured audit events to the logging schema and wire into the existing observability pipeline (topic: audit.guardian.v1)
Console/CLI: add request flow and visible session indicators (active guardian, expiry, approvers)
Post-incident playbook: build automation to generate review tickets, attach relevant logs, and kick off key rotation tasks
Testing: create integration tests that simulate emergency workflows and validate audit output and rotation hooks
Docs & runbooks: publish the Guardian Runbook, oncall checklist, and developer guidance in Confluence
decisions: Default TTL set to 15 minutes after stakeholder review; renewals allowed but require fresh approval
Dual-approval chosen as default; automated approval allowed for declared incident severity >= P0 and when configured by tenant admin
Use KMS-signed ephemeral tokens rather than static superuser passwords to eliminate long-lived credentials
Structured audit schema will be enforced at write-time to prevent partial/ambiguous records
